articles.headline: Chelsea charged by FA over alleged discriminatory chanting
articles.description: Chelsea have been charged by the Football Association after discriminatory chanting was reported during their Premier League game away at Fulham in August.
articles.body:
Chelsea have been charged by the Football Association after discriminatory chanting was reported during their Premier League game away at Fulham in August.

Following the team's 3-2 win over their west London rivals on the season's opening weekend, the club issued a statement to their fans warning them against "sectarian chanting."

Victory at Craven Cottage came courtesy of goals from João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer but the club have now been charged with failing to ensure the behaviour of their supporters.

An FA statement read: "Chelsea FC has been charged with breaching FA Rule E21 during the ninth minute of its Premier League fixture against Fulham FC on 24 August.

"It's alleged that the club failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way. It's further alleged that this behaviour was discriminatory in that it included a reference, whether express or implied, to religion or belief."

The day after the match, Chelsea issued a statement to fans who had been in attendance, which read: "The passion and backing from our fans are vital in achieving a successful season, and we encourage you to continue your vocal support for the team.

"Following the fixture, we have received multiple reports of sectarian chanting from a small portion of those in attendance at the match.

- Transfer value tiers: Which club has the most players worth £100M-plus?

- Andre Villas-Boas hits back at John Terry's plane story: 'I see it different'

- Estêvão on reduced game time at Chelsea: 'I try to seize every opportunity I have'

"We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic. Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium.

"Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us tackle discriminatory chanting."

Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your start/sit questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Friday of the NFL's regular season. 

What's the latest injury buzz as kickoff time approaches? Which player is the better bet for your flex spot? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action.

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Bijan Robinson, Falcons offense back in a big way
articles.description: Michael Penix Jr. returned to action and elevated the entire Falcons offense in upset win over Packers in Lambeau.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 25: Bijan Robinson, Falcons offense back in a big way

by Adam Rank

Is Michael Penix Jr. the MVP of the NFL? I mean, the dude might have a case right now after what the Atlanta Falcons did to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night. There hasn't been an upgrade this significant and this fast since Laney Boggs got rid of the glasses and paint-soaked smock in "She's All That." But it's hard to ignore how good the Falcons looked on Thursday night. Let's take a look at some of the numbers from an incredible game. Well, incredible if you're both a fan of an NFC North team (like me) and also started Bijan Robinson.

Robinson had 213 scrimmage yards with a pair of touchdowns for 35.3 fantasy points. Drake London finished with just 194 receiving yards on 9 catches for 28.4 points. I mean, it seems paltry in comparison (it doesn't). Both guys were on fire. It was the third time they each had more than 150 in a single game. The Falcons were the first visiting team at Lambeau Field to produce a 150-yard rusher and receiver.

For Robinson, it was his third game with 200 yards from scrimmage since 2023, tying Jonathan Taylor for the most during that span. All three of these games have been in primetime.

The Falcons found the red zone! The Falcons went 27 drives without reaching the red zone to start the season, but they made up for it after finally breaking the skid on the third drive of the game. But be honest, you were nervous when Penix opened the game with the interception? It's ok, we were all a little nervous.

Some other good news is that London and Kyle Pitts Sr. combined for 214 receiving yards! All right the four points from Pitts wasn't ideal. I do have more hope that he's going to break out of his season-opening skids. I mean, four points seem massive compared to where he was to start the season. But Penix makes this offense more dynamic and raises the bar for everyone.

London has 100 receiving yards in six of his past seven games with Penix.

The Packers were still able to put up big numbers for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Which is what we are really concerned about here, right? Watson became the first Packers receiver to open the season with a touchdown in three consecutive games since Davante Adams in 2018. Golden was targeted 12 times and turned that into 5 receptions for 100 yards and a touchdown.

The Packers are putting up some fantasy numbers, which is great. But if this offense is truly going to get rolling again, it needs to run the football. The Packers rushed for 17 yards on Thursday night

articles.headline: José Mourinho on 'non-negotiable' rules for Real Madrid to follow: 'Don't betray me'
articles.description: José Mourinho has spoken about his managerial philosophy, warning of the importance of trust between players and coach -- and "non-negotiable" rules for his squad to follow -- as he looks to build a new winning team at Real Madrid.
articles.body:
José Mourinho has spoken about his managerial philosophy, warning of the importance of trust between players and coach -- and "non-negotiable" rules for his squad to follow -- as he looks to build a new winning team at Real Madrid.

Veteran coach Mourinho returned to the Bernabéu this summer -- 13 years after he was last in charge -- after Madrid went two years without landing a major trophy, and fired two coaches, Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa, last season.

He's had a tricky start to life back in Spain, though, with Madrid already six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona and having lost last weekend's derby to Atletico.

"Don't betray me," Mourinho told the Bet It Drives Show, when asked about trust and management. "When I say don't betray me, of course, I'm speaking about football. Don't betray me, and I'll always be there for you."

Mourinho has had a reputation as a strict disciplinarian, but has claimed he's now more "calm" at this stage of his career.

"There are rules that are not negotiable," Mourinho said. "If you report at 9 a.m., it's 9 a.m. for everybody. If you arrive at 9.15, even if you're a superstar, you just can't. I don't accept it ... But another thing is giving them freedom to express themselves."

Madrid's 2025-26 season was disrupted by a number of off-field issues with critics citing a lack of training-ground discipline, including a clash between Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde which saw the latter hospitalised.

"You are a football player 24 hours a day," Mourinho said. "Everything reflects the job. What you eat, what you drink, how you sleep, even things in your private life. You cannot ski. You cannot ride a bike.

- European Golden Shoe: Who's leading Raphinha, Mbappé, Haaland in race for top goal award?

- Marc Cucurella 'sent a subtle message' to try to tempt Rodri into Real Madrid move

- Transfer value tiers: Which club has the most players worth £100M-plus?

"You fall off your bike, and you don't play three matches maybe, or maybe worse, maybe you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player. If you feel it's a hobby, you're dead. There's always a relationship between what you achieve and what you give up."

Mourinho also discussed the process behind his surprise return to Madrid, where he had a successful, but turbulent, first spell.

"After two seasons where the biggest club in the world didn't have the best results and a little 'divorce' with the fans, the club contacted me," he said. "They told me 'We know you. You know us. You know the club, you know the culture.

"We need you. We need you to rebuild. We need you to start again an amazing decade that the club had. We need a person with your profile.'"

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026: League execs examine top 100 countdown, race for No. 1
articles.description: ESPN's NBA Rank 2026 countdown is in the books, but debates are just beginning -- on social media and around the league.
articles.body:
Nothing in the NBA world inspires heated debate like ESPN's annual ranking of the 100 players for the upcoming season.

After NBA Rank 2026 came out earlier this week, New York Knicks guard Josh Hart unleashed a little sarcasm in response to landing at No. 89.

"They [are] always wrong," Hart wrote on social media. "I should be at least No. 88."

The newly minted champion was hardly the only person in the league to raise objections with the results during a year that lacked consensus.

With help from an informal survey of a dozen NBA executives and league personnel, let's run through some of the biggest ranking arguments and critiques that emerged this week to set the table for the 2026-27 season and clear up misconceptions.

NBA Rank 2026:

Top 10 players | Nos. 11-50 | Nos. 51-100

Roundtable: Was LeBron ranked too low?

Top 100 audit: What NBA Rank got wrong

10 players already on the radar for 2027

The battle for No. 1

ESPN's seven-person voting panel was split between three players for the No. 1 spot: Nikola Jokic prevailed with 694 points in the vote, narrowly topping Victor Wembanyama (693) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (691).

Similarly, the survey of front office executives returned passionate arguments for all three players to be considered the best in the world.

Jokic's supporters highlighted his statistical production and offensive orchestration, while Wembanyama's fans pointed to his two-way impact and San Antonio's 62-win season in 2025-26, and Gilgeous-Alexander's backers focused on his back-to-back MVP awards and leadership.

"Jokic makes his whole team better than anyone else," one general manager said. "If you gave him and Wemby the same teammates, Denver would be better. Wemby being young doesn't bother me. What bothers me is that he made young mistakes in the playoffs."

Still, plenty of league executives agreed with ESPN's insiders that the 22-year-old Wembanyama's time is now.

"Look at how fast he is improving," one general manager said. "If you're looking ahead to where we'll be [after the 2027 playoffs], he's got to be No. 1. He could be No. 1 for the next five years."

With Jokic posting triple-doubles and Wembanyama leading the NBA in several defensive metrics, a Gilgeous-Alexander backer argued that the conversation should be about more individual numbers.

"He's the most complete player in the world," the executive said. "Production, leadership, emotional intelligence. List all the boxes that a star should check, and he checks the most."

Two more No. 1 candidates

After Jokic, Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander, ESPN's voting panel had a noticeable gap before the second tier, which included Luka Doncic at No. 4 and Giannis Antetokounmpo at No. 5.

Though most of the informal survey respondents agreed with the main three candidates, one league executive argued that Doncic should be included in the top tier and will end the season at No. 1.

articles.headline: What to know before setting your lineup for Week 3: One last chance for Loveland, Herbert
articles.description: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 3.
articles.body:
I still can't believe that I bought into the Los Angeles Chargers this summer ... but I honestly should have seen this coming. Jim Harbaugh is an eclectic dude. So is Mike McDaniel. QB Justin Herbert is dating pop star Madison Beer. I mean, this reads more like the plot of a Lifetime football movie than the makeup of a championship-caliber football team. It makes the plot of "Draft Day" seem believable. Well, maybe outside of a GM trading the sixth overall pick in the draft for three years of second-round picks.

All that said, I'm kind of down with the Chargers this week. Because every time the world is ready to bury the Chargers, they always seem to rise to the occasion. 

I'm giving one last run for Herbert, even though I'd probably be better with options like Bryce Young, who has been a popular pickup over the past two weeks on the waiver wire. Young has recorded two of his five best fantasy performances this season alone. He started in just 9% of ESPN leagues in Week 2. I suspect that number is significantly higher this week. 

Here are some other notes to get you ready for Week 3 of the season. 

Quarterback notes

Jared Goff has scored at least 20 fantasy points in five of his last six games. He wasn't even being drafted as a QB1 this year, but he's going to be carrying a lot of fantasy teams for the rest of the season. 

Patrick Mahomes is the victim of having a matchup that's too good. People are afraid the Kansas City Chiefs will be so far ahead so early that they won't throw the ball. But tell me, how will the Chiefs get all of those points? I'm all-in on Mahomes, who is averaging 21 fantasy points per game since the start of last season, second among quarterbacks. 

Geno Smith has the best matchup for any quarterback this week, as the Detroit Lions have been very generous to opposing quarterbacks. Is this the kind of thing that will blow up in my face? Yeah, probably. I'm using him as a straight injury replacement, as I'm not ready to bench Herbert for him. But if you had one of the many quarterbacks who are now out this week, let's go! 

Running back notes

Running backs struggled in Week 2, with only eight scoring at least 15 fantasy points. The best of the top runners last week was Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, a guy who kind of drifted through fantasy drafts but has been massive in the early going of the season. This week he gets the Houston Texans, who have allowed the third-fewest points to running backs.

Speaking of Houston, David Montgomery struggled a bit in Week 2 and rushed the ball just six times, a significant drop-off from his Week 1 performance when he had three total touchdowns. He will bounce back this week against the Colts, who have been one of the most generous defenses to opposing quarterbacks, running backs, receivers ... everything. They give up points to everyone.

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups for Week 3: Stroud, Wicks, Spears among top options
articles.description: If injuries or tough matchups have you seeking help, Matt Bowen provides options at each key position.
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

With a brutal run on quarterback injuries in Week 2 -- Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Jaxson Dart -- there's a need for the position in deeper leagues and 2QB/superflex formats. So, that's where we'll start, with four available quarterbacks to check out. Plus, I have a group of wide receivers, with two ascending players and a high-upside target. As always, we'll hit on the running backs and tight ends, while ending with a defense in a prime matchup.

Quarterbacks

C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans (36.4% rostered; at Colts)

Stroud would be a fringe QB1 for me in shallower leagues this week if Nico Collins (hamstring) is cleared to go. Even if not, I still see value here as a streaming option versus an Indianapolis Colts defense that ranks in the bottom five against QBs, giving up a league-worst 337.5 passing yards per game. Stroud has scored at least 16 fantasy points in both games this season, and the Texans will look to create more offensive balance against the Colts after attempting 55 passes in their Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Stroud can be started in deeper formats.

Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks (26.9% rostered; at Commanders)

I'd get Darnold (glute) in the lineup this week if he's ready to roll, given the matchup versus the Washington Commanders. This defense gave up four touchdown passes to Dak Prescott in Week 2 and has allowed a league-high seven through two games. Darnold will take his shots to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. And if Darnold isn't cleared, then I would pick up Drew Lock (3.7% rostered). The Seahawks' No. 2 quarterback threw three touchdowns and accumulated 21.4 fantasy points against the Arizona Cardinals last week.

Geno Smith, New York Jets (6.0% rostered; at Lions)

Smith hasn't produced big numbers over his first two games (12.4 fantasy PPG), and he has thrown only one touchdown pass. But the matchup works here versus a struggling Detroit Lions defense, one that is missing its difference-makers in the secondary. Detroit has given up a league-high 32.0 fantasy PPG to opposing quarterbacks. Sure, Smith isn't on the same level as Josh Allen, who scored 40.82 points versus the Lions last week. However, Smith will have opportunities to attack coverage voids Sunday at Ford Field.

Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (8.8% rostered; at Saints)

articles.headline: Barcelona's pursuit of Julián Álvarez is 'in the past' - Deco
articles.description: Barcelona sporting director Deco says the club's pursuit of Julián Álvarez is "in the past" after it emerged the Spanish champions would have to raise money through player exits to be able to sign the Atlético Madrid striker in January.
articles.body:
Barcelona sporting director Deco says the club's pursuit of Julián Álvarez is "in the past" after it emerged the Spanish champions would have to raise money through player exits to be able to sign the Atlético Madrid striker in January.

Barça spent the summer trying to sign Álvarez from Atlético, failing with a bid of over €100 million ($113.9m) as their LaLiga rivals refused to engage in any form of negotiations.

Sources told ESPN the door was not completely closed on Álvarez potentially moving to Spotify Camp Nou in the future, but Deco has appeared to close it for now.

"Julián Álvarez is the past," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit this week.

"Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn't possible in the end. We made an offer. [Atlético] said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions.

"I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club."

Barça signed Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal late in the summer transfer window after failing to land Álvarez, although it's Raphinha who has stepped up as the team's No.9 so far this season.

Following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, the Brazil winger has been reconverted into a striker to great effect, scoring 14 goals in eight appearances.

That has lessened the need to sign a new forward in January, especially given Barça treasurer Ferran Olivé has confirmed the club would have to move players on in order to afford Álvarez.

"We can make signings in January because the financial situation is positive now, but we would probably have to sell first," Olivé said.

"That's how the rules work in LaLiga. For someone to come in, others have to leave. We have a small excess [within the league-imposed spending cap] of around €3-4m ($3.4m-4.5m,) which would allow us to do a small deal."

- Barcelona sporting director: No interest in Man United's JJ Gabriel

- José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid

- Lamine Yamal rejects goal stats for Ballon d'Or for 'players that make you dream'

Asked if Álvarez would be possible, Olivé added that an operation for the Argentina forward "would not fit" at the moment.

Álvarez, 26, has been left in a difficult situation at Átletico after publicly revealing he wanted to leave the club this summer.

That resulted in him being jeered during the home game against Villarreal in August by his own team's supporters.

In total, he has made four appearances for the club this season, starting just one game, after being a regular during his first two campaigns after joining from Manchester City in 2024.
